subject: Money
title: Lender of Last Resort
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lender of Last Resort.

hook.text: In a crisis, only the central bank can create unlimited money instantly. This power prevents total collapse.

buildup.text: When banks can't borrow from anyone, the central bank steps in. It lends when nobody else will.

discovery.text: Walter Bagehot wrote the rule in 1873: lend freely, at a penalty rate, against good collateral.

twist.text: In 2008, the Fed lent to insurance companies and car makers—far beyond Bagehot's rules. The line expanded.

climax.text: The lender of last resort is a promise: the system won't collapse. But that promise makes risk-taking easier.

punchline.text: The safety net exists. Banks know it.

quiz.question: Who formulated the classic rules for the lender of last resort?
